finding: Position leak: in the raw files the preferred reply is always `chosen` (label would be 100% one class)
decision: Swap A/B by hash(pair_id) in step 5; label share is now 49.8% in train

finding: Rule violations differ by subset (quarantine rate: chi2 p = 5.6e-65, Cramer's V = 0.042): 'missingness' is not MCAR
decision: Quarantine with reason + source line (not silent drop); report quarantine rate per subset every run
limitation: Rates are small; the reason why subsets differ (collection process) cannot be tested from the data

finding: 93% of pairs share their opening prompt; 92.2% of official test pairs have their prompt in official train
decision: Keep the group split (step 7) instead of the official split; contract rule 'no group_id in two splits'
limitation: Grouping on the first turn cannot catch paraphrased prompts

finding: 0.2% of train pairs have near-identical replies (similarity >= 0.9)
decision: Keep them (real comparisons) but add an evaluation slice for near-identical pairs in M3
limitation: Labels on almost-equal replies are the noisiest; they cap achievable accuracy

finding: Reply length is right-skewed (skew 2.02 -> -0.39 after log1p); the 1.5 IQR fence would flag 5.0% of replies
decision: Flag (not delete) replies above the train 99th percentile; use log1p lengths for numeric features
limitation: Long replies are valid data; flagging is only for evaluation slices

finding: Inputs are related: reply A vs B length rho = 0.50, turns vs context words rho = 0.82
decision: Use the log length ratio (step 11) rather than two raw lengths for linear baselines; keep both for slices

finding: Rows are clustered in prompt groups: resampling groups instead of rows inflates the variance of the length-bias estimates (median design effect 1.085); the effect still holds and replicates on held-out dev (helpful-base: confirmed, helpful-rej.-sampled: confirmed, helpful-online: confirmed, harmless-base: confirmed)
decision: Report group-bootstrap intervals (resampling prompt groups) for M3 test accuracy, not row-level intervals
limitation: Per-subset test accuracy will only be known to about +/-5%

finding: Random-row and prompt-group 5-fold CV agree (gap 0.2%) for the length x subset and bag-of-words models; group folds vary more between folds; dev: length x subset 57.9%, bag of words, reply A - reply B 54.8%
decision: Use GroupKFold for any cross-validation in M3; the bag-of-words model is the first text baseline
limitation: No leak for reply-only features; a model that reads the prompt could still memorise it

decision: Model inputs keep the last 256 words of the context (step 11, left truncation)
limitation: Early turns are lost for long conversations

finding: The longer reply is preferred in 58.2% of helpful-base pairs and 42.1% of harmless-base pairs (Cramer's V = 0.144; opposite sides of 50%); pooled: 51.8%
decision: Length is a shortcut: never report pooled accuracy alone; evaluate per subset and per length-gap slice
limitation: Association, not causation: length may stand for informativeness or for refusing

finding: Length alone scores 51.4% on dev when pooled, but 58.2% with one length model per subset (majority class: 48.3%)
decision: Baselines for M3: the reward model must beat the per-subset length model on every subset, not just pooled
limitation: Dev only (test untouched); dev CI is about +/-1.8 points

finding: The text mixes typographic and straight apostrophes (47% vs 13% of replies), so the v1.0 refusal regex missed most refusals; v1.1 flags 2.2% of train pairs
decision: Keep the text as is (ids stay stable); every regex accepts both apostrophes; refusal phrases rebuilt from the most common harmless-base openings in train
limitation: Flag = refusal or non-answer; precision checked only by the manual review sheet

finding: When only one reply is flagged as a refusal, it is preferred in 75% of harmless-base pairs and 27% of helpful-base pairs
decision: Refusal is a second subset-dependent shortcut: report accuracy on the refusal slice per subset in M3 (helpfulness vs harmlessness trade-off)
limitation: Small n outside harmless-base; regex flag, not a human judgement
